summary: Kamala Tiyavanich works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Toronto around 1969–1970, Brown University, and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Ram Chandra Dwivedi. He held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and visited Marburg University in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After earning his PhD at the University of Prague, he held posts there, at the Czech Oriental Institute, and as professor at Utrecht University (~1977–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, University of the Punjab, University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University. She later held academic appointments at Harvard University and the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi (1935–2021) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Akademi, and Advisor at the IGNCA (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia under David F. Germano and Paul Groner, and held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (b. 1965) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Su Bai and served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (b. 1932) works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, becoming Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta (~1968).
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who worked as an instructor at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin (attested 1976).
Kang Youwei (1858–1927) was a Chinese philosophy and sinology scholar. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890, held a post there from around 1891 to 1898, and taught Qichao Liang.

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yün-hua Jan (attested 1976), later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

Kang-yuan Sung is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary (attested 1999) under supervisor Anthony W. Barber and also studied under Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, studied at the University of Paris (~1928–1930), and held an appointment at the Tokyo Imperial Household Museum.
Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied under Acharya Tulsi and held a position as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He founded the University of Lucknow and held a post there (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, and held leadership roles at the IGNCA and India International Centre.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk and Palacký Universities, founded Masaryk University, and taught at Palacký, Cambridge, and Durham University (1969–1990), with visiting roles in India, Sri Lanka, and Korea.
Karen Cheatham is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree from the Graduate Theological Union and a doctoral degree from the University of Toronto (attested 2007).
